`fix` (`api`): **Surface series whose only candidate has ambiguous per-episode coverage**:

`VideoReleaseGroupingService.Group()` correctly collapses files that agree
on group/version/location into a single candidate, but `MightHaveMultipleCandidates`,
`ComputeCandidates`, and the `Series` list endpoint all required more than
one candidate before a series would surface in Release Management. That
hid series whose files merge into one candidate but still leave an episode
covered by more than one file with nothing to distinguish them (an
untagged v2) — observed live with `Sousou no Frieren (2026)`, whose
episodes 9 and 10 each had 2 files from the same release and never
appeared at all.

`MightHaveMultipleCandidates` now flags any episode covered by two
distinct video files regardless of version/location agreement, and the
new `HasAmbiguousEpisodeCoverage` lets `ComputeCandidates` keep a
single-candidate series when that candidate has such an episode, so
`ReleaseCandidate.EpisodeCoverage`'s `PlaceIDs` can do what it was built
for. Removed the now-unused `VideoLocal_PlaceRepository` dependency from
the grouping service.

`feat` (`api`): **Show variations that fit an existing release candidate**:

Variations (`VideoLocal.IsVariation`) were previously excluded wholesale
from `ReleaseManagementController`'s candidate grouping unless
`includeVariations=true`, even when a variation covered the same episode
as a file already shown in a candidate. That's the same "two valid files
for one episode" situation as a multi-part release, just caused by an
unmarked re-release rather than an intentional split — it should be
visible the same way.

`VideoReleaseGroupingService.GetFileDisplaySignals` computes a single
video's quality signals and episode coverage outside the grouping
pipeline (factored out of `BuildSignature` via a shared `ComputeQualityCalc`
helper so the two paths can't drift). `ReleaseManagementController` uses it
to build `ReleaseCandidate.DisplayOnlyFile` entries for a series' variation
videos; `ReleaseCandidate.FromCandidate` attaches one to a candidate only
when its episode coverage overlaps that candidate's own, tagged via the new
`File.IsVariation` flag. A variation matching none of a series' candidates
stays hidden, same as today, unless `includeVariations=true`.

This is deliberately display-only: variations attached this way are always
`IsRedundant = false` and never enter `ComputeCandidates`'s
grouping/redundancy pipeline, so `Preview`/`Execute` deletion and the
background auto-management job are unaffected — they already ignore
variations unconditionally.

`feat` (`api`): **Expose PlaceIDs per episode on ReleaseCandidate**:

When a single release candidate has multiple files covering the same
episode (a multi-part release, or the grouper's "ambiguous" full-collision
case such as an untagged v2), `EpisodeCoverage` previously gave no way for
a client to tell there was more than one file without cross-referencing
every `File.Episodes` list. `PlaceIDs` now lists every `File.PlaceID` that
covers each episode, so a client can show all included files instead of
only surfacing one.

`fix`: **Correct season and year classification for anime with partial or overlapping dates**:

Season windows overlapped a full month with the next season, double-counting
late-season premieres. A null EndDate was also treated as "still airing" for
Movie/OVA/Web/Other/MusicVideo, which AniDB rarely populates for those types,
spreading them across every season/year up to the present. Added
`AniDB_Anime.EffectiveEndDateForSeasons` to fall back to AirDate for those
types, and fixed the same duplicated null-EndDate bug in Years/Stat_AllYears.

`fix` (`api`): **Filter release groups to only existing files in series file summary**:

`Overview.ReleaseGroups` in the WebUI series file summary included
release groups from all `StoredReleaseInfo` records for the anime,
regardless of whether the corresponding files still existed on disk.
Filtered the release groups to only those whose (ED2K, file size) key
matches a file with a valid physical location, matching the behavior of
`StoredReleaseInfoRepository.GetUsedReleaseGroups()`.

`fix` (`api`): **Persist new group before updating children in group manager**:

When creating a new group via the group manager, the group was not
saved to the database before its children/series relationships were
updated, causing foreign key failures. Saved the group first when its
`AnimeGroupID` is 0 (new entity).

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Add shoko-build CLI tool for plugin builds**:

Introduces Shoko.BuildTools, a dotnet tool that wraps MSBuild with
assembly metadata injection, source-level auto-tag discovery, manifest
management, and release packaging.

- Injects PackageID/Name/Overview, dependencies, tags, runtime
  identifier, and git metadata into the built DLL as assembly metadata
- Auto-discovers Shoko service interface implementations (IReleaseInfoProvider,
  IHostedService, etc.) using Roslyn syntax trees and prepends them as tags
- Manages manifest.json: creates/updates release entries with download
  URLs and SHA256 checksums, with per-channel pruning support
- Packs build output into a .zip archive
- Supports multi-RID builds (reads RuntimeIdentifiers from the project)
- Template substitution for {runtime}, {version}, {name}, {abstraction}
  in --url and --output arguments
- Auto-detects manifest.json in CWD, project directory, or parent
- Publishes to NuGet as a global tool (shoko-build)

Server-side changes:
- PluginManager reads embedded PackageID/Name/Overview and dependencies
  from assembly metadata, preferring them over IPlugin instantiation
- Warning logged when embedded metadata is missing
- Embedded identity used in failure fallback paths (legacy namespace,
  ABI mismatch, missing dependencies) instead of generated stubs
- Error messages const-ified for reuse

Closes workflow integration with daily and release pipelines.

`feat` (`api`): **Add plugin dependency resolution and lifecycle enforcement**:

Introduces a full plugin dependency system across the server, API, and
SignalR layers.

Data models:
- PluginDependency type (PluginID, VersionRange, IsOptional) in
  Shoko.Abstractions
- Dependencies lists on LocalPluginInfo, PackageReleaseInfo, and
  RemotePackageReleaseInfo
- RemotePackageDependencyInfo for manifest JSON deserialization

Resolution service:
- IPluginDependencyResolver interface with ResolveDependencies,
  GetDependents, GetUninstallCascade, ValidateEnable/Disable methods
- PluginDependencyResolver implementation with version range parsing
  (>=, ^, ~, exact), transitive cascade traversal, and cycle detection

Lifecycle enforcement (PluginController):
- Enable blocked by missing dependencies (412 Precondition Failed)
- Disable blocked by dependents (409 Conflict) unless Force=true
- Uninstall shows cascade and requires force=true

Install integration (PluginPackageController):
- autoResolveDependencies query parameter on install endpoint
- Missing dependencies return 424 Failed Dependency unless auto
  resolving

API endpoints:
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/{id}/Dependencies — resolved dependency tree
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/{id}/Dependents — reverse dependency list
- GET /api/v3/Plugin/DependencyGraph — full graph

SignalR:
- PluginEventEmitter broadcasts plugin:installed / plugin:uninstalled
  events via AggregateHub

`feat` (`api`): **Add SemanticVersion JSON converter for extended version formats**:

Introduces a custom JSON converter that parses version strings in
formats like 1, 1.0, 1.0.0, 1.0.0.0, and 1.0.0-dev.N into System.Version.
The -dev.N suffix maps to Revision, matching the existing
ToSemanticVersioningString convention.

- SemanticVersionConverter (STJ) and SemanticVersionNewtonsoftConverter
  applied to RemotePackageReleaseInfo.Version
- Updates InstallPackageByID version parsing to use the new converter
  instead of the hacky .Replace("-dev.", ".") workaround
- Schema version pattern updated: up to 4 numbers for stable, up to 3
  numbers plus -dev.N for dev. Prevents 4-part versions with dev suffix
- Channel description documents that -dev.N is only valid for Dev channel

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Add Shoko.BuildTools.Targets NuGet package for MSBuild metadata injection**:

Introduces Shoko.BuildTools.Targets, a development-dependency NuGet
package that auto-injects assembly metadata at build time for Shoko
plugins.

Three MSBuild tasks:
- StampGitMetadata — runs git commands to capture release date, source
  revision, and release tag; writes them as AssemblyMetadata attributes
- ReadPluginManifest — reads manifest.json for PackageID, PackageName,
  PackageOverview, tags, and dependencies; writes as .cs assembly info
- ReadPluginIdentityFromSource — Roslyn-based fallback when no manifest
  exists; parses source files to extract the IPlugin class, resolves
  literal GUIDs, and calls UuidUtility.GetV5 via reflection against the
  referenced Shoko.Abstractions for computed GUIDs

Auto-injects RuntimeIdentifier ("any" for portable libraries) via
static ItemGroup.

Server project updated:
- References Shoko.BuildTools.Targets package
- CorePlugin.StaticID changed from runtime GetV5 computation to
  hardcoded UUIDv5 value

Workflow updates:
- buildtools-targets-nuget job added to daily and release pipelines

`fix` (`db`): **Make NHibernateDependencyInjector's type-info caches thread-safe**:

`Instantiate()` runs concurrently across NHibernate sessions on different
worker threads. Its two static type-info caches (`s_allTypes`,
`s_typeHasValidConstructors`) were plain `Dictionary`s with an
unsynchronized check-then-add pattern:

    if (!s_typeHasValidConstructors.TryGetValue(clazz, out var hasParameters))
    {
        hasParameters = ...;
        s_typeHasValidConstructors.Add(clazz, hasParameters);
    }

Two threads racing on the same not-yet-cached `clazz` both miss the
`TryGetValue` and both call `.Add()` concurrently, corrupting the
dictionary's internal state (`InvalidOperationException: Operations
that change non-concurrent collections must have exclusive access`).
The corruption is permanent for the process's lifetime — every
subsequent `Instantiate()` call touching that dictionary throws until
the process restarts, cascading into any code path that instantiates
an NHibernate entity (observed via TMDB metadata jobs and the Lua
renamer's `Studios` access).

The race window only opens right after a restart, before the caches
warm up, which is why this went unnoticed since it was introduced in
2023 (`4e720796f`) — it needs concurrent first-time access to the same
entity type in that narrow window, which a startup job backlog makes
far more likely than steady-state traffic.

Swapped both caches to `ConcurrentDictionary`.

`fix`: **Close remaining static-field race flagged by SonarCloud (S2696)**:

s_allTypes was still built via `??=` on a static field from an instance
method — a second, narrower race than the one this PR already fixes:
concurrent first callers could each build and assign their own
ConcurrentDictionary independently. Harmless in practice (last write
wins, no corruption), but the same "static field written from an
instance method needs its own synchronization" reasoning applies, and
SonarCloud flagged it as CRITICAL (S2696) on this PR's diff.

Switched to LazyInitializer.EnsureInitialized, which guarantees the
dictionary is built and assigned exactly once regardless of concurrent
first access.

`fix` (`db`): **Handle null RenamerInstance Settings in migration**:

The MigrateRenamers migration crashed when a RenamerInstance had null
Settings in the database:
1. ConvertToJson(null) returned empty string, then JsonNode.Parse('')
   threw JsonReaderException — only MessagePackSerializationException
   was caught, so it escaped to the outer handler
2. SaveFailedRenamerItem passed null bytes to File.WriteAllBytes,
   throwing ArgumentNullException

Guard the JSON operations behind a null/empty check on Settings
instead of catching the secondary exception. Write an empty file
for null settings so the restorer can produce a null-config preset.
The ProcessConfigs restorer now treats 0-length .messagepack files
as null configuration instead of moving them to .error.
